home.title: Scheduled clicks. Recurring prompts.
home.lead: ScheduledClicker v1.2.0 is a free, local desktop tool for Windows 11 and macOS 13+. Schedule a mouse click or repeat prompt input and Send clicks, with five languages and light/dark appearance.
download.title: Download ScheduledClicker v1.2.0
download.lead: Choose Windows EXE or Mac ZIP. Both are the latest stable release. No GitHub account is needed. Opening instructions and checksums are directly below each platform choice.
windows.title: Scheduled clicks and prompt loops for Windows
windows.lead: Download the portable Windows 11 EXE. Use exact-time or delayed clicks and bounded prompt loops in one window, with five languages and light/dark controls.
macos.title: Scheduled clicks and prompt loops for Mac
macos.lead: One universal app for macOS 13 or later, on Apple silicon and Intel. Download the ZIP, move the app to Applications, then grant Accessibility permission.
loop.title: Set up a recurring prompt loop
loop.lead: Repeat one prompt or a sequence with a round limit or deadline. This guide covers position capture, a real trial, waiting, pause and cancellation on Windows and Mac.
codex.title: Schedule a continuation prompt for Codex
codex.lead: Use ScheduledClicker to enter a continuation prompt at a chosen time. It performs local clicks and pasting; it does not detect AI progress or usage-limit resets.
safety.title: Download verification, permissions and limits
safety.lead: Understand clipboard use, stopping behavior, tested scope and unsigned downloads before using ScheduledClicker v1.2.0 with another app.
faq.title: ScheduledClicker questions and answers
faq.lead: Find the current Windows and Mac files, understand installation warnings, and learn how languages, appearance, prompt loops and cancellation work.
changelog.title: ScheduledClicker version history
changelog.lead: v1.2.0 is the latest stable release for both platforms. Earlier versions are historical downloads; this website update does not change the released apps.
modes.title: Two modes in one window
modes.text: Simple mode schedules one single or double click at a future local time or after a delay. Loop mode pastes the same prompt or a sequence, clicks Send and repeats within configured limits. Both modes share a live clock, language picker and theme button.
languages.title: Five languages, with manual switching
languages.text: The app starts in Traditional Chinese for any Chinese system locale, including Simplified Chinese; Japanese, Korean and German select their matching language, and all others select English. Switch languages in either mode. This website offers the same five languages through the links at the top; each language has its own shareable pages.
theme.title: Light and dark appearance
theme.text: The app reads the system appearance when it opens. The sun/moon button switches both modes for the current session; restarting reads the system preference again.
prompt.title: Your edited prompts stay yours
prompt.text: Only the untouched initial prompt follows language changes: 繼續, Continue, 続けて, 계속 or Weiter. Once you edit or delete it, the app preserves your text. A running schedule keeps the prompt captured when it started.
limits.title: Keep the target visible and unchanged
limits.text: Keep the computer awake and unlocked, with the target window, input and conversation unchanged. Fixed coordinates cannot identify a different conversation or moved field. A Send click does not prove delivery. The app does not inspect AI replies, bypass usage limits or detect reset times.
privacy.title: Local operation and the clipboard
privacy.text: The app has no network access, account, ads or telemetry. Loop mode overwrites the system clipboard and does not restore its previous contents; text may remain in clipboard history or the target draft. Simple mode does not use the clipboard. Mac Copy diagnostics also replaces it when you press that button. Schedules and positions are not saved across restarts.
interval.title: When does the interval begin?
interval.text: The wait starts after each round completes. At least one maximum-round or deadline limit is required; if both are enabled, the first reached stops the loop. The action delay between clicks and pasting is separate from the wait between rounds. The interval is not synchronized with an AI service's quota window.
stop.title: Pause, cancel and emergency stop
stop.text: Pause between rounds preserves the remaining wait for Resume; the deadline still applies. Pausing during a round stops it. Cancel, F8 (Fn+F8 on some Mac keyboards) or closing the app stops remaining steps but cannot undo pasted text or completed clicks. Inspect the draft before restarting to avoid duplicates.
tested.title: What was verified?
tested.text: The owner accepted Mac build12004 functionality and Windows prompt-language, custom-text preservation and loop trial checks. Both platforms passed automated builds, scheduling, localization and UI checks. This does not establish every third-party app, display setup, permission-denial path or physical emergency-stop scenario.
compatWin.title: Windows compatibility
compatWin.text: Simple mode supports exact future time or a delay of one second to 168 hours. Position capture takes three seconds. Per-monitor DPI and negative screen coordinates are supported. Input runs at normal user privilege; an app running as administrator may reject it. Windows 11 is the documented target.
compatMac.title: Mac permissions and controls
compatMac.text: Accessibility permission is required to control another app. Loop mode requests it before capture; simple mode checks before scheduling input. Capture both points in the same regular accessible app window. Support is not restricted to Safari. Numeric duration, action-delay and round-count fields support typing, mouse wheel and trackpad adjustments.
files.title: Which file do I need?
files.text: Choose ScheduledClicker.exe for Windows or ScheduledClicker-macOS-universal.zip for Mac. Apple silicon and Intel use the same ZIP. The .sha256 files are text checksums, not apps. GitHub's Source code ZIP/TAR files contain source, not the ready-to-run app. Official release downloads do not require sign-in.
warning.title: Why does the system show a warning?
warning.text: The Windows EXE is unsigned. The Mac app is ad-hoc signed, not Developer ID signed or Apple-notarized. An unfamiliar-publisher warning is different from a malware, damaged-file or organization-policy block. Follow the matching instructions below; do not disable system protection to run the app.
installWin.steps: Download ScheduledClicker.exe using the Windows button. Keep it in a local folder where you want to run it; there is no installation wizard.
Verify the downloaded file using the Windows instructions below, then double-click the EXE.
If the app opens, choose Simple mode and test one harmless click first. Test a loop on disposable text before using a real conversation.
installWin.warning: If SmartScreen says Windows protected your PC because the app is unrecognized, confirm the official download and checksum first. If you choose to proceed and Windows offers it, select More info → Run anyway. This unsigned build may display Unknown publisher. If the message reports malware, an antivirus detection or a managed-device restriction, stop and use the report link or contact your administrator. Do not turn off SmartScreen or antivirus; a matching checksum alone does not prove safety.
installMac.steps: Download ScheduledClicker-macOS-universal.zip using the Mac button and verify the ZIP before extracting it. If Safari already extracted the download, you may already have ScheduledClicker.app; keep or download the original ZIP if you want to verify its checksum.
Double-click the ZIP to extract it if needed. In Finder, drag ScheduledClicker.app into Applications. There is no PKG installer and no separate Apple silicon download.
Open the app from Applications. If macOS cannot verify the developer or notarization, review the specific opening instructions below.

Open System Settings → Privacy & Security → Accessibility. Enable ScheduledClicker; if it is missing, use + and select the app in Applications. Approve with your Mac credentials if requested, then quit and reopen ScheduledClicker if the permission is not recognized.

Choose Simple mode for a harmless click test. For a loop, capture the input and Send positions in the same visible target window and try one round with disposable text. Permission allows control of other apps; grant it only if you trust this app.
installMac.warning: For an unidentified-developer or unnotarized-app warning, first try opening the app once. If you trust this official download, go to System Settings → Privacy & Security, find the message about ScheduledClicker and choose Open Anyway, then confirm Open if offered. Do not use this as a remedy for a malware or damaged-app warning; stop and report the exact message instead. Do not disable Gatekeeper or remove quarantine with a terminal command.
installMac.replacement: Replacing a preview or older copy? Quit the old app before moving the new copy into Applications. Check Accessibility again: if the enabled entry points to the old copy and permission still fails, remove that entry and add the current app from Applications, then reopen it. Capture positions again. v1.2.0 uses Mac build12004; these are the release version and internal build number, not two different downloads.
verify.intro: A checksum checks that your bytes match the published file; it does not independently establish trusted authorship. Download the matching .sha256 file and open it as text. Compare its 64-character hash with your command result; uppercase/lowercase does not matter. If they differ, do not open the app: download again from the official link and report a repeated mismatch.
verify.win: Windows: open PowerShell. Replace the example path with the EXE's actual location (File Explorer → right-click the file → Copy as path). Run the command below and compare the Hash field with ScheduledClicker-Windows.sha256. Use the full path so your current PowerShell folder does not matter.
verify.mac: Mac: open Terminal. Type shasum -a 256 followed by a space, drag the original ZIP from Finder into Terminal to insert its full path, then press Return. Compare the first 64 characters with ScheduledClicker-macOS-universal.sha256. If you type a path yourself, put quotes around paths containing spaces.

loop.steps: Open Loop mode. Set the first run, wait after each round and delay between actions.
Enable a maximum round count, a deadline or both. For a first trial, use one round and disposable text.
Choose the same prompt every round or edit a sequence. Choose whether to repeat the final prompt when the sequence ends. Replacement of existing input is optional; the default inserts at the cursor.
Capture the input field and Send button, each after its three-second countdown. Keep both in the same visible window and keep that window in place.
Try one round and review the confirmation. This really pastes text and clicks Send. Check the target result before starting the schedule; a completed click count is not a delivery receipt.
support.title: Need help opening or using the app?
support.text: Report a problem on GitHub Issues (a GitHub account is required to post). Include Windows/macOS version, app version/build, target app, reproduction steps and the full error. On Mac, Copy diagnostics can supply build and execution-stage details; inspect it before posting. Do not include prompts, private conversations or personal file paths in public reports. If you have no account, check the FAQ and existing issues first.
support.diagnostic: Copy diagnostics does not collect prompt text or window titles, but it includes OS, target app and process/window identifiers. Review the content before sharing. Copying it overwrites the clipboard.
upgrade.title: Upgrading from an older version
upgrade.text: Quit the old app and replace it with the official v1.2.0 file. You do not need Actions artifacts or a GitHub account to download. Schedules and captured positions do not persist; set them again. Keep the old file separately only if you need a rollback. Historical versions do not include all current loop features.
codex.text: Prepare the continuation prompt, keep the intended Codex conversation visible, then use the loop guide to capture input and Send. Choose a bounded interval that suits your own workflow. ScheduledClicker is an independent tool, is not affiliated with OpenAI, and cannot guarantee that Codex is ready or that a usage window has reset.
